ecosystem.notes: Gross Bookings include Freight revenue, which Uber books gross, as well as taxes, tolls and fees. They exclude tips. Revenue includes Freight revenue. The 10-K does not state total driver or courier earnings, so payouts is null. 'Platform Participant direct transaction costs' (costs paid to Platform Earners that Uber records in cost of revenue, plus end-user incentives) are a partial, mixed amount, not total earnings, and are not used.
ecosystem.ratioNote: Uber presents revenue on a gross basis in markets where it is responsible for the Mobility, Delivery or Freight service, with payments to drivers and carriers in cost of revenue, so revenue ÷ Gross Bookings overstates what Uber keeps.

footprint.notes: No U.S. state breakdown for 2024 exists on uber.com. Checked: Uber's us_en and global_en sitemaps and all 111 English-locale country sitemaps for impact, economic and economy pages (other hits were older country reports, e.g. Canada 2022 and 2023, British Columbia 2023, Bangladesh 2021, plus Uber Eats 2023 merchant reports); /us/en/impact/ has only New York City and Los Angeles city pages, both '2025 in review' (city-level and after the snapshot, so not used; NYC says drivers made close to $4 billion in 2025); state posts on the newsroom date from 2015-2018 (e.g., Florida 2017 earnings) or are advocacy pieces; the U.S. 'Uber in the economy' page cites an undated EDR Group study ($17 billion GDP, $5.7 billion driver value-add 'per year over the study period'), not used. Country rows are Public First estimates commissioned by Uber, each in its own currency, so they are separate metrics and not comparable. CA and NZ amounts appear only as '$' on the local pages and are read as local dollars. India's 'INR 36,000 crores' is a forecast for Auto and Moto only and was skipped. The 18,000 outside-U.S. employees is a region; no U.S. figure was derived.

paidout.notes: Inputs copied from the pilot. Marketplace: salesEnabled = Gross Bookings − revenue. In gross (principal) markets and Freight the fare is in both Gross Bookings and revenue and nets to zero, and driver pay is counted once, through paidOut; in agent markets driver earnings sit outside revenue and are counted once, through salesEnabled. Gross Bookings include taxes, tolls and fees and are before consumer discounts (overstates). Single-year paidOut is about 7% below the accrual cross-check because accrued insurance reserves rose 2.82bn inside operating cash flow.
